optional_codes.reason: The note documents cataract surgery on the left eye in 2019, so the cataract extraction status code is supportable. It is not required, because the provider's stated diagnosis for the left eye, pseudophakia, is carried by Z96.1. Either answer is defensible.

citations.case: ICD-10-CM Tabular List FY2027, inclusion term at H25.1 (nuclear sclerosis cataract); ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines FY2027, Section I.B.13 (laterality: each eye is coded for what is documented in that eye); Section I.C.21 (status codes: presence of an intraocular lens); Section I.B.5 (signs and symptoms integral to a definitive diagnosis are not coded separately); Section IV.G (first-listed: the condition chiefly responsible for the visit)

coder_notes: Right eye: nuclear sclerotic cataract, coded by the inclusion term at H25.1; the note does not use the words age-related. Left eye: pseudophakia, coded as presence of an intraocular lens, which has no laterality. No cataract is diagnosed in the left eye. The 2019 cataract surgery on the left eye may be reported as a status code but is not required (see optional_codes). Blurred vision, glare, night-driving difficulty and reduced acuity are integral to the cataract. Visually significant has no code axis. The normal fundus findings are not coded. Traps: a left-eye or bilateral cataract code because both eyes appear in the note; an unspecified-eye cataract code; a cataract code for the pseudophakic left eye
